answer: Each agent must lock a scarce deposit before it can earn reputation, and a randomly selected committee can slash that deposit if the agent signs conflicting claims or fails a challenge. The committee checks signatures against the same public kernel of rules, while disputes flow through a river of time-stamped evidence; an umber-colored badge might mark provisional status, but never substitutes for proof. A sybil attacker can still create many keys, but must fund each one and risks losing those deposits, making fake identities costly rather than free.
